reason: Three of the five sub-claims verify and two do not. Verified by driving the master: the publish eyebrow renders "WHAT LANDS IN THE MESSAGE" and the body directly beneath opens "This is what lands in the message." — the heading printed twice on one screen, six words apart, which no studio at this bar ships. The second eyebrow "The moment it becomes theirs" is CAPTIONS.publish in render-core.js ("the moment it becomes theirs") lifted verbatim from the showroom onto the product surface, and since round 1's fix renamed the destructive control to "Delete this moment", "moment" now carries the row-object sense twice on the owner screen against the temporal sense here. On ended, "public" (render-b.js:756) is the only occurrence of that word in the whole master while "shared" carries the same fact one line above (:753) — a genuine fourth vocabulary for one binary, and "Nothing you saw before" does presuppose a prior visit. What is NOT real: the owner-chain half is already handled. Round 1's sharpened fix landed, so the row word is "Shown"/"Hidden", its accessible name ends "Shown to guests.", and the editor segment reads "What guests see :: Shown | Hidden" — one vocabulary, exactly the settlement this finding asks for. The row word being a mono 11px uppercase micro-label sitting under "SAT 1 AUG" is true, but it is the row's only button and its ::after spans the row (inset:0), so "render the word only when the item is hidden" would delete the click target and the keyboard entry point into the editor on six of seven rows. That trades a copy nit for a dead row. And the fix's own ended rewrite is defective twice over: "is not shared here any more" is a word-for-word synonym of "is no longer shared here" (same vocabulary, so it fixes nothing), and "Nothing has been deleted. Only the link stopped working." matches neither branch of interaction-check.mjs:742 /not been deleted|not public/i, so shipping it as written turns the behaviour gate red. Confirmed on the narrowed ground only.
sharpenedFix: Three edits in render-b.js and one in interaction-check.mjs; drop everything the fix proposes for the row and the editor. (1) publish, .b-pressBody: delete the leading "This is what lands in the message. " so it opens "It carries the day, the distance and the plan, and nothing from your workspace: no notes, no suppliers, no prices." (2) publish, second .b-who: replace "The moment it becomes theirs" with "The link", which also stops the product borrowing the lab's caption and leaves "moment" meaning only a row. (3) ended, .b-note: replace "Nothing you saw before has been deleted. It is just not public any more." with "Nothing has been deleted. Only the link stopped working." — this is the one edit that removes the fourth name and the presupposition together. (4) In the SAME change, widen interaction-check.mjs:742 from /not been deleted|not public/i to /nothing has been deleted|not been deleted/i, or step 3 reds the gate; line 740's /turned off/i still passes because the headline is untouched. Leave .b-endedBody exactly as it is: "is no longer shared here" is already the plainer of the two phrasings and the proposed swap is a no-op. Leave the row .b-grab word rendering as is; if the accessible name is worth touching, lead it with the verb only — "Open Menu tasting at The Orchard. Saturday 1 August, in 16 days. Shown to guests." — and keep the button present on every row. Optional new assertion: ended contains neither "public" nor "you saw before", and the publish body does not repeat the string of its own eyebrow.
